title: Gold is yellow because of Einstein’s relativity
body: Most metals look silvery because they reflect all visible colours about equally. Gold is different because its heavy nucleus, with 79 protons, whips its inner electrons to a large fraction of the speed of light. Relativistic effects then shift the energies of its outer electron orbitals, so gold absorbs some blue light. The reflected light is missing blue, so our eyes read it as warm yellow; without relativity, gold would look much like silver.

slides.heading: Electrons near light speed
slides.text: In gold, the innermost electrons move at roughly half the speed of light. That pulls the outer 6s orbital closer to the nucleus.

slides.heading: Blue gets absorbed
slides.text: The shrunken 6s and expanded 5d orbitals sit closer in energy, so gold absorbs blue light. In silver that gap is larger, so silver reflects all colours.

slides.heading: Mercury and your car
slides.text: Similar effects weaken bonding in mercury, helping keep it liquid. Calculations suggest about 10 V of a 12 V lead–acid car battery is due to relativity.
